newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serb university official hurt in bombing - agency.
newsitem.headline: Serb university official hurt in bombing - agency.

text.p: The Serb rector of Pristina University in Serbia's Albanian-majority province of Kosovo was seriously injured in a car bomb attack on Thursday, the Bosnian Serb news agency SRNA reported.

Local authorities could not immediately be reached to verify the incident. But a Reuters Television cameraman contacted by telephone said the rector, Radivoje Papovic, was taken to hospital after the attack.

SRNA, official news agency of the nationalist Serb republic entity in neighbouring Bosnia, blamed the reported car bombing on ethnic Albanian "terrorists". Kosovo's Albanians have been seeking autonomy from centralised Serbian rule for years.
SRNA quoted its correspondent in Pristina, Kosovo's largest city, as saying Papovic was "seriously injured this morning in the explosion of a car bomb planted by Shqiptar ethnic Albanian terrorists".

"The explosive in a parked Opel Kadett in Pristina's Zivojina Misica street was most probably activated by remote control when Papovic was driving by in his official car," SRNA reported. "Both cars were completely destroyed in the blast."
SRNA quoted eyewitnesses as saying Papovic suffered serious head injuries but there were still no official reports on his condition from Pristina hospital, where he was being treated.
